review: 1:1–2 בּוֹטֵחַ … נִשְׁעָן — the Arabic pairs two verbs (وَاثِق / مُتَّكِل), and the Hebrew keeps both, as Isa 26:3–4 sets בָּטוּחַ beside the Rock that endures.

1:3 כָּל־הַבְטָחָה … נֶאֱמָנָה — the Arabic كُلُّ وَعْدٍ مِنْكَ صَادِق is singular 'every promise is true'; the Hebrew keeps the singular noun with a singular predicate rather than 'all Your promises are true', so each promise is weighed on its own.
2:4 אֶשְׁקֹט — Isa 30:15 (בְּהַשְׁקֵט וּבְבִטְחָה תִּהְיֶה גְבוּרַתְכֶם); the rest is the promised quiet, not a mood, which is why the verb is kept rather than 'ארגיש שלווה'.
3:4 עַד־הַקֵּץ — Matt 28:20 (וְהִנֵּה אָנֹכִי אִתְּכֶם כָּל־הַיָּמִים עַד־קֵץ הָעוֹלָם); the Hebrew stops at הַקֵּץ as the Arabic stops at الْمُنْتَهَى, without adding 'of the world'.
4:2 בְּפוֹדֶה כָּל־בָּשָׂר — the Arabic مُفْتَدِي الْأَنَام is 'Redeemer of mankind'; בָּשָׂר is kept in the Joel 3:1 sense of all flesh, so the title stays universal without becoming abstract.
